title: Quasar shift handoff brief — evening into overnight (Nov 9 2028)
content:
Summary:
- Shift: Quasar (evening -> overnight), coverage 18:00 — 02:00 PT. Handoff from Ravi to Maya at 18:00. Light traffic overall but with one notable incident (INC-2341) that produced elevated tail latency for hosted-api text-generation routes between 18:22 and 19:05 PT.

Key events (timeline):
- 18:05 PT: Pre-handoff quick check: all clusters nominal. No alerts.
- 18:22 PT: Pager alert (p95 latency > 1200ms) for route /v1/generate (eu-west-1). First spikes noticed by synthetic checks.
- 18:24 PT: On-call (Ravi) triaged — identified correlation with cache-miss pattern on prefix cache for a small subset of customers.
- 18:31 PT: Failed autoscaler pod restart observed on a single Dedicated pool (ded-gpu-pool-3) — crashloop back-off tied to a model loader OOM in the runtime.
- 18:40 PT: Mitigation: temporarily routed traffic for affected route to warm fallback model variant (model-v2-quant) in us-west-2; latency returned to 200–400ms for rerouted traffic.
- 18:55 PT: Applied temporary runtime config: increased kv-cache-size for affected model shards on eu-west-1 nodes (hotfix).
- 19:05 PT: SLOs recovered, alerts cleared.

Impact:
- Affected customers: ~6 customers in eu-west-1 saw 3–7% error-rate increase and elevated p95 for ~40 minutes. No data loss; all requests were served (some rerouted). Business impact classified as P2.

Root cause (hypothesis):
- Primary: sudden prefix cache eviction storm concurrent with a model loader memory regression after a recent runtime change (PR #789) that changed per-shard prefetch behavior. The prefetch increase pushed one of the smaller Dedicated nodes above its usable memory footprint and caused repeated OOM restarts for the runtime process.
- Secondary: autoscaler attempted to replace crashing pods but new pods hit the same loader OOM before lifecycle probes marked them ready, creating capacity gap for a few minutes.

Actions taken (during shift):
- Immediate: traffic steering to fallback model-v2-quant; created temporary route override in routing policy (Ravi).
- Hotfix: increased kv-cache-size per shard (Maya applied via infra-runbooks -> runtime-config set), which reduced cache churn and cache miss amplification.
- Rollback candidate: identified PR #789 as risky; reverted the prefetch change in a test pool staging-1 and reproduced OOM locally. Revert PR queued (owner: Liam).
- Pager follow-ups: created INC-2341 with full timeline and pointers to logs.

Post-incident follow-ups (owners + ETA):
- Liam O'Neill: revert prefetch change in runtime (PR revert + smoke test) — target: 2028-11-10 11:00 PT.
- Aisha Gómez: add pod lifecycle probe tweak + pre-start memory sanity check in Dedicated pool helm charts — target: 2028-11-11.
- Ops: create safelist for automatic fallback routing for high-impact customers to avoid reroute surprise — target: 2028-11-13.
- SRE: schedule deeper heap profile of model loader on a replicated infra workload (attached to INC-2341) — owner: Maya — target: 2028-11-12.

Runbook deltas (proposed):
- Add explicit "model loader OOM" section: reproduce steps, required heap-dump commands, k8s probe adjustments, and quick routing rollback commands. (Drafted; see linked PR).
- Add automated check: when pod restarts > 3 within 5m for runtime role => autoscaler should not immediately scale down other pools (prevents capacity oscillation). (owner: SRE infra team).
- Add emergency command snippets to the handoff template (below) for quick routing switches and cluster-safe JVM/Python heap toggles.

Tasks for next shift (priority order):
1) Monitor eu-west-1 for recurring OOMs (dashboards: infra/runtime-eu-west-1, alert rule: runtime.probes.ooms).
2) Confirm revert PR results in staging and coordinate rollout window if safe.
3) Run the memory-health job against a 10% traffic synthetic in dedicated pool to validate fixed prefetch behavior.
4) Close INC-2341 after RCA doc is attached and owners ACK.
5) Follow up with product-eng for impacted customers' compensations/notifications (CS coordinating).

Quick checks for next on-call (commands / dashboards):
- kubectl -n infra get pods -l role=runtime | grep CrashLoopBackOff
- ./scripts/collect-heap-dump.sh <pod> (run as admin-if-needed)
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/d/runtime-eu-west-1, https://grafana.redwood/d/latency-hosted-api
- Alerts to watch: runtime.loader.oom, routing.p95.high, autoscaler.scale-fails

Escalation contacts (order):
1) Eng SRE lead: Aisha Gómez (pager)
2) Runtime owner: Liam O'Neill (Slack @liam)
3) Platform infra on-call: Derek Huang (pager)
4) Customer success escalation: Harpreet Singh (email + pager)

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why did the prefetch change disproportionately affect a single Dedicated pool? Hypothesis: skewed shard placement + slightly older NVIDIA driver on those nodes — need driver inventory.
- Are there other models with similar prefetch settings that we didn't catch in canary? Need a sweep across model catalog.

Notes to next on-call (Maya -> next):
- If you see rising p95 again in eu-west-1, prioritize routing to fallback model first; do not attempt immediate autoscaler restarts on ded-gpu-pool-3 until heap dump completes.
- Use the emergency route-override (policy id: routing-override-ops-2028) — it will not trigger billing anomalies for test tenants.
- Keep customer comms draft (attached in INC-2341) ready for CS if they ask.

Things I scribbled (notes-to-self style):
- Consider adding a nightly health job that runs a small synthetic workload exercising prefetched weights to surface OOMs earlier.
- Add driver-version check to node exporter (quick metric).
- Double-check node taint rules for ded-gpu-pool-3 (it had a manual taint applied last month during maintenance).

Attachments / links inside incident:
- heap-dump logs (s3://redwood-ops/heapdumps/2028-11-09/), runtime logs slice: s3://redwood-ops/runtime-logs/2028-11-09/inc-2341.log
- Reproduction notes in linked PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/789

Signing off (handover):
- On-call end: 02:00 PT. Next on-call: Riya Menon (03:00 PT local sync scheduled).
- I will be available in #sre-quasar for 30m after handoff for quick questions.

-- Maya
